node-1.label: 19-year-old female presented with left-sided chest pain and cough, then six weeks later had right lateral chest wall pain, shortness of breath, and menorrhagia after starting rivaroxaban

node-2.label: Initial presentation: 19-year-old female presented to emergency room with left-sided chest pain and cough; CT imaging identified multiple pulmonary emboli in the left inferior segmental pulmonary arteries; no provoking factors or other complications at that time; discharged on rivaroxaban with hemoglobin 14.9 g/dL and platelet count 402 per uL.

node-3.label: Six weeks later, she returned with right lateral chest wall pain and shortness of breath; hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL, platelet count 485 per uL; she reported developing menorrhagia after starting rivaroxaban.

node-4.label: Follow-up CT imaging showed a new pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe segmental pulmonary arteries and decreased clot burden in the left inferior segmental pulmonary artery branches; she received packed red blood cell transfusion and was started on heparin drip; no signs of heart failure or hypoxia; started on norethindrone for menses suppression.

node-5.label: Laboratory tests showed ferritin 6.8 ng/mL and she received an iron transfusion; she was transitioned to warfarin; one month later hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, ferritin 36.1 ng/mL, iron saturation 25%, and platelet count 566 per uL.

node-6.label: Hypercoagulable workup including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, prothrombin gene mutations, lupus anticoagulant, cardiolipin antibodies, and beta-2 glycoprotein antibodies was unrevealing; testing for JAK2, MPL, CALR, and JAK2 exon 12-15 mutations was negative; subsequent CSA revealed heterozygous variant of unknown significance Chr1(GRCh37):g.43805172C>A predicted to result in glutamine to lysine substitution at codon 208 in exon 4 of MPL gene, not reported as associated with a clinical condition according to HGMD; father was being treated for a similar condition.

attrs.why: node-2 unprovoked PE and node-4 new PE on anticoagulation support; node-6 negative standard workup refutes known thrombophilia.

Original support from elevated platelets, MPL VUS, and family history is now substantially weakened by new bone marrow biopsy findings showing normocellular marrow with mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia and no dysplasia, which favor reactive thrombocytosis over MPL/MPN. Laboratory physician analysis also favors reactive thrombocytosis. Negative JAK2/CALR mutations further refute this hypothesis. Confidence reduced from 0.5 to 0.2.

Original support from menorrhagia after rivaroxaban, Hb 6.6, iron deficiency, and transfusion remains strong. Laboratory physician analysis concludes the overall picture best fits rivaroxaban-induced anemia. New bone marrow findings of reactive thrombocytosis are consistent with iron deficiency anemia, further supporting this hypothesis. Confidence remains 0.9.

node-10.label: Bone marrow biopsy shows normocellular marrow with mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia and no dysplasia
